source: US DOL OFLC, PERM permanent labor certification disclosure files

files_skipped.reason: no column for CASE_STATUS, EMPLOYER_NAME, CITIZENSHIP

caveats: A PERM certification is an employer asking to sponsor someone for permanent residence after testing the local labor market. It is not a hire, not an admission, and not an H-1B petition.
Many of these workers were already in the job on another visa. The visa_held field says which one.
Citizenship is published for FY2013 onward and was removed from FY2025, when the form lost every worker field at once. Birth country runs FY2015 to FY2024. The series has ended.
No worker is named in the federal file and none is named here. Employer, job title, worksite and citizenship are all published disclosure.
Employers are matched on the name as filed, so one body can appear under several spellings and any single total is a floor.
Sponsoring a worker is lawful. Nothing here says otherwise.

anomaly_notes.sponsored_while_not_work_authorised: The worker held a visa class that is not work authorisation when the employer filed. Lawful in itself; the opposite of the ordinary path.
anomaly_notes.citizenship_differs_from_birth_country: Citizenship and country of birth are different fields and they disagree on this row. Common and unremarkable for many people; it is here because the two are often assumed to be the same thing.
anomaly_notes.a_us_citizen_named_on_the_filing: The filing records the worker as a US citizen. A US citizen needs no labor certification, so the field is almost certainly wrong. It is published as filed.
anomaly_notes.job_title_unique_in_its_sector: A job title filed exactly once by any employer in this sector. Usually a local naming quirk rather than a strange job.
